			<commonInfo>
				<para>This default BREX data module is provided with Issue 4.2 of S1000D. It contains in total 261 rules consisting of: <randomList>
						<listItem>
							<para>firm rules expressed in the specification text, not supported by the schema structures, however, such that they can be represented by an XPath expression and such that a CSDB object can be automatically be verified against these XPath rules</para>
						</listItem>
						<listItem>
							<para>narrative rules expressed in the specification text, not supported by the schema structures, and not possible to formalize in an XPath expression, hence, not useful in an automatic rules checking procedure</para>
						</listItem>
					</randomList>
				</para>
				<para> The highest rule number is 00268.</para>
				<para>CPF 2009-039S1 introduced an attribute valueTailoring (on element objectValue) specifying to which degree a certain BREX data module may adjust the use/interpretation of a given value, e.g. a configurable attribute. The values are specified as follows (refer to Chap 4.10.2.2): <randomList>
						<listItem>
							<para>
								<emphasis>restrictable</emphasis> - a BREX at a lower level may impose further restrictions to the given value by changing the textual interpretation to reflect that restriction</para>
						</listItem>
						<listItem>
							<para>
								<emphasis>lexical</emphasis> - a BREX at a lower level may adjust the text string constituting the interpretation, however, only in respects that do not in any way change the conceptual and semantic meaning of the interpretation</para>
						</listItem>
						<listItem>
							<para>
								<emphasis>closed</emphasis> (default value) - a BREX at a lower level must not in any way restrict or alter the interpretation of a value declared at a higher level.</para>
						</listItem>
					</randomList>
				</para>
			</commonInfo>

				<simplePara>Specify allowable values of new configurable attribute brStatus</simplePara>

			<commonInfo>
				<para>This default BREX data module is provided with Issue 4.2 of S1000D. It contains in total 261 rules consisting of: <randomList>
						<listItem>
							<para>firm rules expressed in the specification text, not supported by the schema structures, however, such that they can be represented by an XPath expression and such that a CSDB object can be automatically be verified against these XPath rules</para>
						</listItem>
						<listItem>
							<para>narrative rules expressed in the specification text, not supported by the schema structures, and not possible to formalize in an XPath expression, hence, not useful in an automatic rules checking procedure</para>
						</listItem>
					</randomList>
				</para>
				<para> The highest rule number is 00268.</para>
				<extra_id_5>CPF 2009-039S1 introduced an attribute valueTailoring (on element objectValue) specifying to which degree a certain BREX data module may adjust the use/interpretation of a given value, e.g. a configurable attribute. The values are specified as follows (refer to Chap 4.10.2.2): <randomList>
						<listItem>
							<para>
								<emphasis>restrictable</emphasis> - a BREX at a lower level may impose further restrictions to the given value by changing the textual interpretation to reflect that restriction</para>
						</listItem>
						<listItem>
							<para>
								<emphasis>lexical</emphasis> - a BREX at a lower level may adjust the text string constituting the interpretation, however, only in respects that do not in any way change the conceptual and semantic meaning of the interpretation</para>
						</listItem>
						<listItem>
							<para>
								<emphasis>closed</emphasis> (default value) - a BREX at a lower level must not in any way restrict or alter the interpretation of a value declared at a higher level.</para>
						</listItem>
					</randomList>
				</extra_id_5>

      <wiringFields>
         <descrWire>
            <descrCircuitIdent>
               <fieldName>Circuit code</fieldName>
               <descr>Circuit code identifies the system or circuit to which the wire belongs.</descr>
            </descrCircuitIdent>
            <descrWireNumber>
               <fieldName>Wire number</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire number contains the most specific part of the identification of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireNumber>
            <descrSectionIdent>
               <fieldName>Wire section identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire section identification identifies different sections of wires which are connected by non-functional breaks.</descr>
            </descrSectionIdent>
            <descrWireType>
               <fieldName>Wire type</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire type gives information on the type of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireType>
            <descrWireGauge>
               <fieldName>Wire gauge</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire gauge contains the gauge of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireGauge>
            <descrPartNumber>
               <fieldName>Wire part number</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire part number contains the project specific part number of a wire.</descr>
            </descrPartNumber>
            <descrHarnessIdent>
               <fieldName>Harness identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness identification contains the identification of the harness to which a wire belongs.</descr>
            </descrHarnessIdent>
            <descrWireSeqNumber>
               <fieldName>Wire sequential number</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire sequential number contains the sequential number of a wire, which can be part of the entire wire identification.</descr>
            </descrWireSeqNumber>
            <descrWireInfoCircuitIdent>
               <fieldName>Wire information circuit code</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire information circuit code contains the identification of the system or circuit to which the wire belongs.</descr>
            </descrWireInfoCircuitIdent>
            <descrWireInfoSectionIdent>
               <fieldName>Wire section identification (for the wire information branch)</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire section identification (for the wire information branch) contains the identification of different sections of wires which are connected by non-functional breaks.</descr>
            </descrWireInfoSectionIdent>
            <descrEmcCode>
               <fieldName>Electromagnetic compatibility code</fieldName>
               <descr>Electromagnetic compatibility code identifies the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) classification of a wire.</descr>
            </descrEmcCode>
            <descrLength>
               <fieldName>Wire length</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire length contains the length of a wire.</descr>
            </descrLength>
            <descrWireColor>
               <fieldName>Wire color</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire color identifies the color of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireColor>
            <descrTwist>
               <fieldName>Twist information</fieldName>
               <descr>Twist information contain information about the twisting of a wire. Twist information can be different on both sides of a wire.</descr>
            </descrTwist>
            <descrCoaxialCableFlag>
               <fieldName>Coaxial cable flag</fieldName>
               <descr>Coaxial cable flag identifies a wire as coaxial cable.</descr>
            </descrCoaxialCableFlag>
            <descrTriaxialCableFlag>
               <fieldName>Tri-axial cable flag</fieldName>
               <descr>Tri-axial cable flag identifies a wire as tri-axial cable.</descr>
            </descrTriaxialCableFlag>
            <descrSignalInfo>
               <fieldName>Signal information</fieldName>
               <descr>Signal information identifies the signals on a wire. This can be the signal name, the effective voltage, the effective current or the waveform of the signal.</descr>
            </descrSignalInfo>
            <descrFunctionalItemRef>
               <fieldName>Functional item reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Functional item reference identifies an electrical equipment to which a wire extremity is connected.</descr>
            </descrFunctionalItemRef>
            <descrContact>
               <fieldName>Contact</fieldName>
               <descr>Contact describes the contact identification.</descr>
            </descrContact>
            <descrWireConnectionCode>
               <fieldName>Wire connection code</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire connection code is used for generic identification of the electrical potential to which a wire end is connected in the related sub elements. It is used for data processing purposes.</descr>
            </descrWireConnectionCode>
            <descrNetworkAnalysisCode>
               <fieldName>Network analysis code</fieldName>
               <descr>Network analysis code describes the behavior of the wire end in the network connection analysis in relation to other wires via the equipment. It is used for data processing purposes.</descr>
            </descrNetworkAnalysisCode>
            <descrGroupCode>
               <fieldName>Group code</fieldName>
               <descr>Group code indicates the physical grouping of wires connected to the same contact.</descr>
            </descrGroupCode>
            <descrScreen>
               <fieldName>Screen information</fieldName>
               <descr>Screen information contains information about the type of the wire in a shielding situation and the identification of the screen to which the wire end is connected.</descr>
            </descrScreen>
            <descrPreparationInfo>
               <fieldName>Preparation information</fieldName>
               <descr>Preparation information gives the preparation information for wires before connecting to a contact.</descr>
            </descrPreparationInfo>
            <descrFinishingInfo>
               <fieldName>Finishing information</fieldName>
               <descr>Finishing information gives the finishing information for the connection of wires to a contact.</descr>
            </descrFinishingInfo>
            <descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
               <fieldName>Responsible partner company information</fieldName>
               <descr>Responsible partner company information indicates the company or the organization, which is responsible for the wire data.</descr>
            </descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
            <descrRouting>
               <fieldName>Routing</fieldName>
               <descr>Routing gives routing information of a wire via clipping points and special components (eg, current transformers, panels or bungs), through which wires pass in the related sub elements.</descr>
            </descrRouting>
            <descrFeedThru>
               <fieldName>Feed-thru information</fieldName>
               <descr>Feed-thru information identifies equipment through which a wire passes.</descr>
            </descrFeedThru>
            <descrWireRoute>
               <fieldName>Wire route lane code</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire route lane code identifies the lane of the primary systems with a code where the wire is routed.</descr>
            </descrWireRoute>
            <descrRestriction>
               <fieldName>Restriction</fieldName>
               <descr>Restriction gives restrictions concerning the wire.</descr>
            </descrRestriction>
            <descrNextHigherAssy>
               <fieldName>Next higher assembly information</fieldName>
               <descr>Next higher assembly information identifies the physical or logical assembly of which a wire is a part.</descr>
            </descrNextHigherAssy>
            <descrFunctionalDescrRef>
               <fieldName>Functional description reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Functional description reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications for further functional information about a wire.</descr>
            </descrFunctionalDescrRef>
            <descrIllustrationRef>
               <fieldName>Illustration reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Illustration reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications, which show wiring illustrations (eg, circuit or wiring diagrams).</descr>
            </descrIllustrationRef>
         </descrWire>
         <descrHarness>
            <descrHarnessIdent>
               <fieldName>Harness identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness identification contains the identification of a harness.</descr>
            </descrHarnessIdent>
            <descrPartNumber>
               <fieldName>Harness part number</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness part number contains the project specific part number of a harness.</descr>
            </descrPartNumber>
            <descrAltPartNumber>
               <fieldName>Alternative harness part number</fieldName>
               <descr>Alternative harness part number identifies part numbers that can be used alternatively for a harness.</descr>
            </descrAltPartNumber>
            <descrManufacturerCode>
               <fieldName>Harness manufacturer code</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness manufacturer code gives the manufacturer for an alternative harness part number.</descr>
            </descrManufacturerCode>
            <descrHarnessVariantIdent>
               <fieldName>Harness variant identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness variant identification contains the variant of a harness. Improvements during series production or engineering requirements are reasons why different harnesses are used in one type of system.</descr>
            </descrHarnessVariantIdent>
            <descrHarnessVariantIssue>
               <fieldName>Harness variant issue</fieldName>

            </descrHarnessVariantIssue>
            <descrHarnessName>
               <fieldName>Harness name</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness name contains the name of a harness.</descr>
            </descrHarnessName>
            <descrEmcCode>
               <fieldName>Electromagnetic compatibility code</fieldName>
               <descr>Electromagnetic compatibility code identifies the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) classification of a harness.</descr>
            </descrEmcCode>
            <descrMinTemperature>
               <fieldName>Minimum temperature</fieldName>
               <descr>Minimum temperature describes the minimum temperature, for which the harness is approved.</descr>
            </descrMinTemperature>
            <descrMaxTemperature>
               <fieldName>Maximum temperature</fieldName>
               <descr>Maximum temperature describes the maximum temperature, for which the harness is approved.</descr>
            </descrMaxTemperature>
            <descrHarnessEnvironment>
               <fieldName>Harness environment</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness environment contains information concerning the environment in which a harness is located.</descr>
            </descrHarnessEnvironment>
            <descrSleeve>
               <fieldName>Harness sleeve</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness sleeve contains the project specific part number of the harness sleeve.</descr>
            </descrSleeve>

               <descrFrequency>

                  <fieldName>Illustration reference</fieldName>
                  <descr>Illustration reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications, which show illustrations of the wire material.</descr>
               </descrIllustrationRef>
            </descrWireMaterial>

      <wiringFields>
         <descrWire>
            <descrCircuitIdent>
               <fieldName>Circuit code</fieldName>
               <descr>Circuit code identifies the system or circuit to which the wire belongs.</descr>
            </descrCircuitIdent>
            <descrWireNumber>
               <fieldName>Wire number</fieldName>
               <extra_id_13>Wire number contains the most specific part of the identification of a wire.</extra_id_13>
            </descrWireNumber>
            <descrSectionIdent>
               <fieldName>Wire section identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire section identification identifies different sections of wires which are connected by non-functional breaks.</descr>
            </descrSectionIdent>
            <descrWireType>
               <fieldName>Wire type</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire type gives information on the type of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireType>
            <descrWireGauge>
               <extra_id_14>Wire gauge</extra_id_14>
               <descr>Wire gauge contains the gauge of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireGauge>
            <extra_id_15>
               <fieldName>Wire part number</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire part number contains the project specific part number of a wire.</descr>
            </extra_id_15>
            <descrHarnessIdent>
               <fieldName>Harness identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness identification contains the identification of the harness to which a wire belongs.</descr>
            </descrHarnessIdent>
            <descrWireSeqNumber>
               <fieldName>Wire sequential number</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire sequential number contains the sequential number of a wire, which can be part of the entire wire identification.</descr>
            </descrWireSeqNumber>
            <descrWireInfoCircuitIdent>
               <fieldName>Wire information circuit code</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire information circuit code contains the identification of the system or circuit to which the wire belongs.</descr>
            </descrWireInfoCircuitIdent>
            <descrWireInfoSectionIdent>
               <fieldName>Wire section identification (for the wire information branch)</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire section identification (for the wire information branch) contains the identification of different sections of wires which are connected by non-functional breaks.</descr>
            </descrWireInfoSectionIdent>
            <descrEmcCode>
               <fieldName>Electromagnetic compatibility code</fieldName>
               <descr>Electromagnetic compatibility code identifies the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) classification of a wire.</descr>
            </descrEmcCode>
            <descrLength>
               <fieldName>Wire length</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire length contains the length of a wire.</descr>
            </descrLength>
            <descrWireColor>
               <fieldName>Wire color</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire color identifies the color of a wire.</descr>
            </descrWireColor>
            <descrTwist>
               <fieldName>Twist information</fieldName>
               <descr>Twist information contain information about the twisting of a wire. Twist information can be different on both sides of a wire.</descr>
            </descrTwist>
            <extra_id_16>
               <fieldName>Coaxial cable flag</fieldName>
               <descr>Coaxial cable flag identifies a wire as coaxial cable.</descr>
            </extra_id_16>
            <descrTriaxialCableFlag>
               <fieldName>Tri-axial cable flag</fieldName>
               <descr>Tri-axial cable flag identifies a wire as tri-axial cable.</descr>
            </descrTriaxialCableFlag>
            <descrSignalInfo>
               <fieldName>Signal information</fieldName>
               <descr>Signal information identifies the signals on a wire. This can be the signal name, the effective voltage, the effective current or the waveform of the signal.</descr>
            </descrSignalInfo>
            <descrFunctionalItemRef>
               <fieldName>Functional item reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Functional item reference identifies an electrical equipment to which a wire extremity is connected.</descr>
            </descrFunctionalItemRef>
            <descrContact>
               <fieldName>Contact</fieldName>
               <descr>Contact describes the contact identification.</descr>
            </descrContact>
            <descrWireConnectionCode>
               <fieldName>Wire connection code</fieldName>
               <extra_id_17>Wire connection code is used for generic identification of the electrical potential to which a wire end is connected in the related sub elements. It is used for data processing purposes.</extra_id_17>
            </descrWireConnectionCode>
            <extra_id_18>
               <fieldName>Network analysis code</fieldName>
               <extra_id_19>Network analysis code describes the behavior of the wire end in the network connection analysis in relation to other wires via the equipment. It is used for data processing purposes.</extra_id_19>
            </extra_id_18>
            <descrGroupCode>
               <fieldName>Group code</fieldName>
               <descr>Group code indicates the physical grouping of wires connected to the same contact.</descr>
            </descrGroupCode>
            <descrScreen>
               <fieldName>Screen information</fieldName>
               <extra_id_20>Screen information contains information about the type of the wire in a shielding situation and the identification of the screen to which the wire end is connected.</extra_id_20>
            </descrScreen>
            <descrPreparationInfo>
               <fieldName>Preparation information</fieldName>
               <extra_id_21>Preparation information gives the preparation information for wires before connecting to a contact.</extra_id_21>
            </descrPreparationInfo>
            <descrFinishingInfo>
               <fieldName>Finishing information</fieldName>
               <extra_id_22>Finishing information gives the finishing information for the connection of wires to a contact.</extra_id_22>
            </descrFinishingInfo>
            <descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
               <fieldName>Responsible partner company information</fieldName>
               <descr>Responsible partner company information indicates the company or the organization, which is responsible for the wire data.</descr>
            </descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
            <descrRouting>
               <fieldName>Routing</fieldName>
               <descr>Routing gives routing information of a wire via clipping points and special components (eg, current transformers, panels or bungs), through which wires pass in the related sub elements.</descr>
            </descrRouting>
            <descrFeedThru>
               <fieldName>Feed-thru information</fieldName>
               <extra_id_23>Feed-thru information identifies equipment through which a wire passes.</extra_id_23>
            </descrFeedThru>
            <descrWireRoute>
               <fieldName>Wire route lane code</fieldName>
               <descr>Wire route lane code identifies the lane of the primary systems with a code where the wire is routed.</descr>
            </descrWireRoute>
            <extra_id_24>
               <fieldName>Restriction</fieldName>
               <descr>Restriction gives restrictions concerning the wire.</descr>
            </extra_id_24>
            <descrNextHigherAssy>
               <fieldName>Next higher assembly information</fieldName>
               <extra_id_25>Next higher assembly information identifies the physical or logical assembly of which a wire is a part.</extra_id_25>
            </descrNextHigherAssy>
            <descrFunctionalDescrRef>
               <fieldName>Functional description reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Functional description reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications for further functional information about a wire.</descr>
            </descrFunctionalDescrRef>
            <descrIllustrationRef>
               <extra_id_26>Illustration reference</extra_id_26>
               <descr>Illustration reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications, which show wiring illustrations (eg, circuit or wiring diagrams).</descr>
            </descrIllustrationRef>
         </descrWire>
         <descrHarness>
            <descrHarnessIdent>
               <fieldName>Harness identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness identification contains the identification of a harness.</descr>
            </descrHarnessIdent>
            <descrPartNumber>
               <fieldName>Harness part number</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness part number contains the project specific part number of a harness.</descr>
            </descrPartNumber>
            <extra_id_27>
               <fieldName>Alternative harness part number</fieldName>
               <descr>Alternative harness part number identifies part numbers that can be used alternatively for a harness.</descr>
            </extra_id_27>
            <descrManufacturerCode>
               <fieldName>Harness manufacturer code</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness manufacturer code gives the manufacturer for an alternative harness part number.</descr>
            </descrManufacturerCode>
            <descrHarnessVariantIdent>
               <fieldName>Harness variant identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness variant identification contains the variant of a harness. Improvements during series production or engineering requirements are reasons why different harnesses are used in one type of system.</descr>
            </descrHarnessVariantIdent>
            <descrHarnessVariantIssue>
               <extra_id_28>Harness variant issue</extra_id_28>
               <descr>Harness variant issue contains the issue of a harness variant.</descr>
            </descrHarnessVariantIssue>
            <descrHarnessName>
               <fieldName>Harness name</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness name contains the name of a harness.</descr>
            </descrHarnessName>
            <descrEmcCode>
               <fieldName>Electromagnetic compatibility code</fieldName>
               <descr>Electromagnetic compatibility code identifies the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) classification of a harness.</descr>
            </descrEmcCode>
            <descrMinTemperature>
               <fieldName>Minimum temperature</fieldName>
               <descr>Minimum temperature describes the minimum temperature, for which the harness is approved.</descr>
            </descrMinTemperature>
            <descrMaxTemperature>
               <fieldName>Maximum temperature</fieldName>
               <descr>Maximum temperature describes the maximum temperature, for which the harness is approved.</descr>
            </descrMaxTemperature>
            <descrHarnessEnvironment>
               <fieldName>Harness environment</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness environment contains information concerning the environment in which a harness is located.</descr>
            </descrHarnessEnvironment>
            <descrSleeve>
               <fieldName>Harness sleeve</fieldName>
               <descr>Harness sleeve contains the project specific part number of the harness sleeve.</descr>
            </descrSleeve>
            <descrRouting>
               <fieldName>Routing</fieldName>
               <descr>Routing gives routing information of a harness via clipping points and special components (eg, panels or bungs).</descr>
            </descrRouting>
            <descrFeedThru>
               <fieldName>Feed-thru information</fieldName>
               <descr>Feed-thru information identifies equipment through which a harness passes.</descr>
            </descrFeedThru>
            <descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
               <fieldName>Responsible partner company information</fieldName>
               <descr>Responsible partner company information indicates the company or the organization, which is responsible for the harness data.</descr>
            </descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
            <extra_id_29>
               <fieldName>Functional description reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Functional description reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications for further functional information about a harness.</descr>
            </extra_id_29>
            <descrIllustrationRef>
               <fieldName>Illustration reference</fieldName>
               <extra_id_30>Illustration reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications, which show illustrations of the harness (eg, the routing of the harness).</extra_id_30>
            </descrIllustrationRef>
         </descrHarness>
         <descrElectricalEquip>
            <extra_id_31>
               <extra_id_32>Functional item reference</extra_id_32>
               <descr>Functional item reference identifies an electrical equipment.</descr>
            </extra_id_31>
            <descrPartNumber>
               <fieldName>Electrical equipment part number</fieldName>
               <extra_id_33>Electrical equipment part number contains the project specific part number of an electrical equipment.</extra_id_33>
            </descrPartNumber>
            <descrAltPartNumber>
               <extra_id_34>Alternative electrical equipment part number</extra_id_34>
               <descr>Alternative electrical equipment part number identifies part numbers that can be used alternatively for an electrical equipment.</descr>
            </descrAltPartNumber>
            <descrManufacturerCode>
               <fieldName>Electrical equipment manufacturer code</fieldName>
               <extra_id_35>Electrical equipment manufacturer code gives the manufacturer for an alternative electrical equipment part number.</extra_id_35>
            </descrManufacturerCode>
            <descrInstallationLocation>
               <fieldName>Installation location</fieldName>
               <descr>Installation location contains the installation location information of the electrical equipment.</descr>
            </descrInstallationLocation>
            <descrAccessDoorOrPanel>
               <fieldName>Access door or panel</fieldName>
               <extra_id_36>Access door or panel identifies doors or panels to be opened for getting access to the electrical equipment.</extra_id_36>
            </descrAccessDoorOrPanel>
            <descrAssy>
               <fieldName>Electrical equipment assembly</fieldName>
               <descr>Electrical equipment assembly contains assembly information for electrical components in the related sub elements.</descr>
            </descrAssy>
            <extra_id_37>
               <extra_id_38>Next higher assembly information</extra_id_38>
               <descr>Next higher assembly information identifies the physical or logical assembly of which an electrical equipment is a part.</descr>
            </extra_id_37>
            <descrPositionOnNextHigherAssy>
               <fieldName>Position on next higher assembly</fieldName>
               <descr>Position on next higher assembly identifies the position of the electrical equipment within the box or panel. The position is indicated either by a direct position or by grid coordinates.</descr>
            </descrPositionOnNextHigherAssy>
            <descrMaxMountingPositions>
               <fieldName>Maximum number of mounting positions</fieldName>
               <descr>Maximum number of mounting positions contains the number of mounting positions on a next higher assembly.</descr>
            </descrMaxMountingPositions>
            <descrSystemBreakdownCode>
               <fieldName>System breakdown code</fieldName>
               <extra_id_39>System breakdown code identifies the breakdown of the electrical equipment in the system.</extra_id_39>
            </descrSystemBreakdownCode>
            <descrSiblingPlugIdent>
               <fieldName>Sibling plug identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Sibling plug identification contains the identification of the functional item of the mate connector.</descr>
            </descrSiblingPlugIdent>
            <descrTransverseLink>
               <fieldName>Transverse link information</fieldName>
               <descr>Transverse link information provides information about internally or externally realized electrical connections of different contacts/bolts of equipment.</descr>
            </descrTransverseLink>
            <descrConnectionListClass>
               <fieldName>Connection list class</fieldName>
               <descr>Connection list class assigns electrical items to specific classes, eg connectors, switches, relays etc. It is used for data processing purposes.</descr>
            </descrConnectionListClass>
            <descrElectricalContact>
               <fieldName>Contact identification</fieldName>
               <descr>Contact identification gives the identification of an electrical contact.</descr>
            </descrElectricalContact>
            <descrElectricalStateDescr>
               <fieldName>Electrical state description</fieldName>
               <descr>Electrical state description gives the narrative description of an electrical state, for example "ENERGIZED".</descr>
            </descrElectricalStateDescr>
            <descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
               <fieldName>Responsible partner company information</fieldName>
               <descr>Responsible partner company information indicates the company or the organization, which is responsible for the electrical equipment data.</descr>
            </descrResponsiblePartnerCompany>
            <descrEquipName>
               <fieldName>Electrical equipment name</fieldName>
               <descr>Electrical equipment name gives the nomenclature of an electrical equipment, eg CONNECTOR or FRONT LIGHT.</descr>
            </descrEquipName>
            <descrReqQuantity>
               <extra_id_40>Quantity information</extra_id_40>
               <descr>Quantity information contains the number of multiple occurrence electrical equipment installed on the Product.</descr>
            </descrReqQuantity>
            <descrEquipDescrRef>
               <fieldName>Electrical equipment description reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Electrical equipment description reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications for description of an electrical equipment in the related sub element.</descr>
            </descrEquipDescrRef>
            <descrFunctionalDescrRef>
               <extra_id_41>Functional description reference</extra_id_41>
               <descr>Functional description reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications for further functional information about an electrical equipment.</descr>
            </descrFunctionalDescrRef>
            <descrIllustrationRef>
               <fieldName>Illustration reference</fieldName>
               <descr>Illustration reference gives references to other parts of the electrical system publications, which show illustrations of the electrical equipment.</descr>
            </descrIllustrationRef>

            <extra_id_42>

      <description>
         <levelledPara>
            <title>Quick history of the bicycle</title>
            
            <para>Here are the most important steps in the invention of the bicycle:<sequentialList id="SPEC-0008">
                  <listItem>
                     <para>In 1817 a German professor, baron Karl von Drais, created the first two-wheeled bicycle. It had a handlebar, and looked like a bicycle of today, but it didn't have pedals, and it had a wooden body.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>In the 1860s, French inventors added pedals to the front wheel. However, it took a lot of effort to turn the pedals. Later inventors made bikes out of metal only, and made the front wheel very big, giving higher speed. This design was called the penny-farthing bicycle. However, it was difficult to ride, since it could fall easily.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>Several improvements were made in the 1880s and '90s. In 1885, the safety bicycle was invented. This had two wheels the same size so that the rider could sit at a lower height. It was called the safety bicycle because it was much easier to ride than the penny-farthing. Instead of pedaling and steering with the front wheel, the safety bicycle used steering with the front wheel while the pedals turned the back wheel using a chain. Brakes operated by hand levers on some bikes also increased safety.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>In 1888, Scottish inventor John Boyd Dunlop re-invented a type of tire which was filled with air, and this made cycling far more comfortable.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>Soon, the freewheel was invented. This was a device inside the hub of the back wheel that allowed the wheel to spin even if the rider wasn't pedalling. However, this meant the rider could no longer stop the bike by backpedalling. As a result, a different type of brake was invented which could stop the bike if the pedals were turned backwards. Later inventions included better brakes, and gears, which made cycling over hills much easier.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <note>
                        <notePara>During this time the bicycle became very popular. Long-distance racing are quickly developing:<attentionSequentialList id="SPEC-0004">
                              <attentionSequentialListItem id="SPEC-0005">
                                 <attentionListItemPara id="SPEC-0001">Paris-Rouen, as soon as 1869</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Bordeaux-Paris, in May 1891</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Paris-Brest-Paris, in September 1891</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Liège-Bastogne-Liège, in 1892</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Paris-Roubaix, in 1896</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Tour de France, in 1903</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                           </attentionSequentialList>
                        </notePara>
                        
                     </note>
                  </listItem>
               </sequentialList>
               <verbatimText id="SPEC-0009">Source: https://en.vikidia.org/w/index.php?title=Bicycle&oldid=97889</verbatimText>
            </para>
            
            <note>
               <notePara>Bicycles are nowadays one of the main means of transportation in many parts of the world. Its energy efficiency is particularly high. Its practice, cycling, is both<attentionRandomList>
                     <attentionRandomListItem id="SPEC-0003">
                        <attentionListItemPara id="SPEC-0002">a daily use of transport,</attentionListItemPara>
                     </attentionRandomListItem>
                     <attentionRandomListItem>
                        <attentionListItemPara>a popular hobby,</attentionListItemPara>
                     </attentionRandomListItem>
                     <attentionRandomListItem>
                        <attentionListItemPara>and a sport.</attentionListItemPara>
                     </attentionRandomListItem>
                  </attentionRandomList>
                  <verbatimText id="SPEC-0010">Source: https://fr.vikidia.org/w/index.php?title=V%C3%A9lo&oldid=1427276</verbatimText>
               </notePara>
               
            </note>
         </levelledPara>
         <levelledPara>
            <title>Functional description of a bicycle</title>
            <para>Below is a list of the different bicycle components and a functional description of them. <definitionList>
                  <definitionListHeader>
                     <termTitle>Component</termTitle>
                     <definitionTitle>Functional description</definitionTitle>
                  </definitionListHeader>
                  
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Frame</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The frame is the skeleton of the bicycle. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA3" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the frame system.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Wheel</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The wheel is the point of contact between the bicycle and the road for the bicycle to have movement. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA0" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the wheel.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Spokes</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The spokes are thick wires with tension applied that connect the hub to the rim. You can adjust the tension with the nipple on the rim side.</para>
                        
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Hub</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The hub attaches to the center of the wheel where the axle and the bearings are.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Metal rim</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The metal rim is a metal ring that has a U-shaped cross section to hold the spokes on the inner side and the tire on the outer side.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Seat</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The seat, which is also known as the "saddle", is used as the support platform for the person to sit on the bicycle.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Seat post</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The seat post is used as a support post for the seat and to change the height of the seat for the rider.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Handle bar</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The handle bar is a horizontal bar with handles on each end. The handle bar is a steering mechanism that the rider uses to change the direction of the bicycle. The brake levers are also on the handle bar. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="2" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="720" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for information on how to install the handle bar. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="2" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="520" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for information on removing the handlebar.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Handle bar stem</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The handle bar stem (the stem) attaches the handle bar to the steering tube. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="720" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for information on how to install a stem. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="520" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for information on how to remove the stem.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Brake levers</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>When you operate the brake lever, the brake pads move against the wheel to decrease the speed. The brake lever on the left side operates the front brake. The brake lever on the right side operates the rear brake.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Brakes</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>When you operate the brakes, the brake pad moves against the wheel to decrease the speed of the bicycle. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA1" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a description of the braking system.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Shifters</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The shifters are the mechanisms that you use to change the gears on the bicycle. There are 7 different types of shifters that have been developed over the years, but they all have the same functionality. When you operate the shifters, they pull the control cable to move the derailleur towards a larger diameter chain ring. The shifters can also loosen the cable to let the derailleur move towards a smaller diameter chain ring. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA5" subSystemCode="3" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the shifters.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Crank</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The crank moves the power to the chain rings when the pedals operate.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Pedals</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The pedals move the force of movement from the feet to the cranks.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Chain</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The chain moves the power from the chain rings to the cogs on the freewheel. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA4" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="251" infoCodeVariant="B" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for the procedure on how to clean the chain.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Gears</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The gears have different mechanisms that function together to change the speed of the bicycle. These mechanisms include: <randomList listItemPrefix="pf02">
                              <listItem>
                                 <para>the sprockets</para>
                              </listItem>
                              <listItem>
                                 <para>the chain</para>
                              </listItem>
                              <listItem>
                                 <para>the derailleur</para>
                              </listItem>
                           </randomList> Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA5" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the gear system.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Chain rings</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The chain rings (also known as the "chain wheel") pull on the chain when the cranks turn.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Derailleur</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>A derailleur moves the chain from one sprocket to another to change the gears. There are two different types of derailleur, the front and the rear. The highest ratio (highest gear) is when the chain is on the largest sprocket on the front and the smallest at the rear. To get the lowest gear, the smallest sprocket is at the front and the largest at the rear. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA5" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the derailleur system.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
               </definitionList>
            </para>
         </levelledPara>
      </description>
   </content>

      <description>
         <levelledPara>
            <title>Quick history of the bicycle</title>
            
            <para>Here are the most important steps in the invention of the bicycle:<sequentialList id="SPEC-0008">
                  <listItem>
                     <para>In 1817 a German professor, baron Karl von Drais, created the first two-wheeled bicycle. It had a handlebar, and looked like a bicycle of today, but it didn't have pedals, and it had a wooden body.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>In the 1860s, French inventors added pedals to the front wheel. However, it took a lot of effort to turn the pedals. Later inventors made bikes out of metal only, and made the front wheel very big, giving higher speed. This design was called the penny-farthing bicycle. However, it was difficult to ride, since it could fall easily.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>Several improvements were made in the 1880s and '90s. In 1885, the safety bicycle was invented. This had two wheels the same size so that the rider could sit at a lower height. It was called the safety bicycle because it was much easier to ride than the penny-farthing. Instead of pedaling and steering with the front wheel, the safety bicycle used steering with the front wheel while the pedals turned the back wheel using a chain. Brakes operated by hand levers on some bikes also increased safety.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>In 1888, Scottish inventor John Boyd Dunlop re-invented a type of tire which was filled with air, and this made cycling far more comfortable.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <para>Soon, the freewheel was invented. This was a device inside the hub of the back wheel that allowed the wheel to spin even if the rider wasn't pedalling. However, this meant the rider could no longer stop the bike by backpedalling. As a result, a different type of brake was invented which could stop the bike if the pedals were turned backwards. Later inventions included better brakes, and gears, which made cycling over hills much easier.</para>
                  </listItem>
                  <listItem>
                     <extra_id_45>
                        <extra_id_46>During this time the bicycle became very popular. Long-distance racing are quickly developing:<attentionSequentialList id="SPEC-0004">
                              <extra_id_47 id="SPEC-0005">
                                 <attentionListItemPara id="SPEC-0001">Paris-Rouen, as soon as 1869</attentionListItemPara>
                              </extra_id_47>
                              <extra_id_48>
                                 <extra_id_49>Bordeaux-Paris, in May 1891</extra_id_49>
                              </extra_id_48>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Paris-Brest-Paris, in September 1891</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <attentionListItemPara>Liège-Bastogne-Liège, in 1892</attentionListItemPara>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <extra_id_50>Paris-Roubaix, in 1896</extra_id_50>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                              <attentionSequentialListItem>
                                 <extra_id_51>Tour de France, in 1903</extra_id_51>
                              </attentionSequentialListItem>
                           </attentionSequentialList>
                        </extra_id_46>
                        
                     </extra_id_45>
                  </listItem>
               </sequentialList>
               <verbatimText id="SPEC-0009">Source: https://en.vikidia.org/w/index.php?title=Bicycle&oldid=97889</verbatimText>
            </para>
            
            <extra_id_52>
               <extra_id_53>Bicycles are nowadays one of the main means of transportation in many parts of the world. Its energy efficiency is particularly high. Its practice, cycling, is both<attentionRandomList>
                     <attentionRandomListItem id="SPEC-0003">
                        <attentionListItemPara id="SPEC-0002">a daily use of transport,</attentionListItemPara>
                     </attentionRandomListItem>
                     <attentionRandomListItem>
                        <attentionListItemPara>a popular hobby,</attentionListItemPara>
                     </attentionRandomListItem>
                     <attentionRandomListItem>
                        <attentionListItemPara>and a sport.</attentionListItemPara>
                     </attentionRandomListItem>
                  </attentionRandomList>
                  <extra_id_54 id="SPEC-0010">Source: https://fr.vikidia.org/w/index.php?title=V%C3%A9lo&oldid=1427276</extra_id_54>
               </extra_id_53>
               
            </extra_id_52>
         </levelledPara>
         <extra_id_55>
            <extra_id_56>Functional description of a bicycle</extra_id_56>
            <para>Below is a list of the different bicycle components and a functional description of them. <extra_id_57>
                  <definitionListHeader>
                     <extra_id_58>Component</extra_id_58>
                     <definitionTitle>Functional description</definitionTitle>
                  </definitionListHeader>
                  
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Frame</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The frame is the skeleton of the bicycle. Refer to <extra_id_59>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA3" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </extra_id_59> for a functional description of the frame system.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Wheel</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The wheel is the point of contact between the bicycle and the road for the bicycle to have movement. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA0" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the wheel.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Spokes</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The spokes are thick wires with tension applied that connect the hub to the rim. You can adjust the tension with the nipple on the rim side.</para>
                        
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <extra_id_60>
                     <listItemTerm>Hub</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The hub attaches to the center of the wheel where the axle and the bearings are.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </extra_id_60>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Metal rim</listItemTerm>
                     <extra_id_61>
                        <para>The metal rim is a metal ring that has a U-shaped cross section to hold the spokes on the inner side and the tire on the outer side.</para>
                     </extra_id_61>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <extra_id_62>
                     <extra_id_63>Seat</extra_id_63>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <extra_id_64>The seat, which is also known as the "saddle", is used as the support platform for the person to sit on the bicycle.</extra_id_64>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </extra_id_62>
                  <extra_id_65>
                     <listItemTerm>Seat post</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The seat post is used as a support post for the seat and to change the height of the seat for the rider.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </extra_id_65>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <extra_id_66>Handle bar</extra_id_66>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <extra_id_67>The handle bar is a horizontal bar with handles on each end. The handle bar is a steering mechanism that the rider uses to change the direction of the bicycle. The brake levers are also on the handle bar. Refer to <extra_id_68>
                              <extra_id_69>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="2" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="720" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </extra_id_69>
                           </extra_id_68> for information on how to install the handle bar. Refer to <extra_id_70>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <extra_id_71 modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="2" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="520" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </extra_id_70> for information on removing the handlebar.</extra_id_67>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <extra_id_72>Handle bar stem</extra_id_72>
                     <extra_id_73>
                        <extra_id_74>The handle bar stem (the stem) attaches the handle bar to the steering tube. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <extra_id_75>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="720" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </extra_id_75>
                           </dmRef> for information on how to install a stem. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <extra_id_76 modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA2" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="520" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for information on how to remove the stem.</extra_id_74>
                     </extra_id_73>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Brake levers</listItemTerm>
                     <extra_id_77>
                        <para>When you operate the brake lever, the brake pads move against the wheel to decrease the speed. The brake lever on the left side operates the front brake. The brake lever on the right side operates the rear brake.</para>
                     </extra_id_77>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <extra_id_78>Brakes</extra_id_78>
                     <extra_id_79>
                        <extra_id_80>When you operate the brakes, the brake pad moves against the wheel to decrease the speed of the bicycle. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA1" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for a description of the braking system.</extra_id_80>
                     </extra_id_79>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <extra_id_81>Shifters</extra_id_81>
                     <extra_id_82>
                        <para>The shifters are the mechanisms that you use to change the gears on the bicycle. There are 7 different types of shifters that have been developed over the years, but they all have the same functionality. When you operate the shifters, they pull the control cable to move the derailleur towards a larger diameter chain ring. The shifters can also loosen the cable to let the derailleur move towards a smaller diameter chain ring. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <extra_id_83>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA5" subSystemCode="3" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </extra_id_83>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the shifters.</para>
                     </extra_id_82>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <extra_id_84>
                     <listItemTerm>Crank</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>The crank moves the power to the chain rings when the pedals operate.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </extra_id_84>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Pedals</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <extra_id_85>The pedals move the force of movement from the feet to the cranks.</extra_id_85>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <extra_id_86>Chain</extra_id_86>
                     <extra_id_87>
                        <extra_id_88>The chain moves the power from the chain rings to the cogs on the freewheel. Refer to <dmRef>
                              <dmRefIdent>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA4" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="251" infoCodeVariant="B" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </dmRefIdent>
                           </dmRef> for the procedure on how to clean the chain.</extra_id_88>
                     </extra_id_87>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <extra_id_89>
                     <extra_id_90>Gears</extra_id_90>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <extra_id_91>The gears have different mechanisms that function together to change the speed of the bicycle. These mechanisms include: <randomList listItemPrefix="pf02">
                              <listItem>
                                 <extra_id_92>the sprockets</extra_id_92>
                              </listItem>
                              <listItem>
                                 <extra_id_93>the chain</extra_id_93>
                              </listItem>
                              <listItem>
                                 <para>the derailleur</para>
                              </listItem>
                           </randomList> Refer to <dmRef>
                              <extra_id_94>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA5" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </extra_id_94>
                           </dmRef> for a functional description of the gear system.</extra_id_91>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </extra_id_89>
                  <definitionListItem>
                     <listItemTerm>Chain rings</listItemTerm>
                     <extra_id_95>
                        <para>The chain rings (also known as the "chain wheel") pull on the chain when the cranks turn.</para>
                     </extra_id_95>
                  </definitionListItem>
                  <extra_id_96>
                     <listItemTerm>Derailleur</listItemTerm>
                     <listItemDefinition>
                        <para>A derailleur moves the chain from one sprocket to another to change the gears. There are two different types of derailleur, the front and the rear. The highest ratio (highest gear) is when the chain is on the largest sprocket on the front and the smallest at the rear. To get the lowest gear, the smallest sprocket is at the front and the largest at the rear. Refer to <extra_id_97>
                              <extra_id_98>
                                 <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1000DBIKE" systemDiffCode="AAA" systemCode="DA5" subSystemCode="1" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="AA" infoCode="041" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="A" />
                              </extra_id_98>
                           </extra_id_97> for a functional description of the derailleur system.</para>
                     </listItemDefinition>
                  </extra_id_96>
               </extra_id_57>
            </para>
         </extra_id_55>

               <noSpares />
            </reqSpares>
            <reqSafety>
               <noSafety />
            </reqSafety>
         </preliminaryRqmts>
         <mainProcedure>
            <proceduralStep>
               <para>Clean the bicycle.</para>
               <proceduralStep>
                  <para>Clean the bicycle with water.</para>
               </proceduralStep>
               <proceduralStep>
                  <para>Use the brush from the <internalRef internalRefId="seq-0001" internalRefTargetType="irtt05" /> to clean the brakes, the shift levers, the sprockets and the tires.</para>
               </proceduralStep>
               <proceduralStep>
                  <para>Let the bicycle dry.</para>
               </proceduralStep>
            </proceduralStep>
            <proceduralStep>
               <para>Lubricate the bicycle</para>
               <proceduralStep>
                  <para>Spray the <internalRef internalRefId="sup-0001" internalRefTargetType="irtt04" />, to these moving parts: <randomList listItemPrefix="pf01">
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the brake pivots</para>
                        </listItem>
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the derailleur pivots</para>
                        </listItem>
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the derailleur tension guides</para>
                        </listItem>
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the brake lever pivots</para>
                        </listItem>
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the control cables</para>
                        </listItem>
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the gear sprockets</para>
                        </listItem>
                        <listItem>
                           <para>the chain</para>
                        </listItem>
                     </randomList>
                  </para>
               </proceduralStep>
               <proceduralStep>
                  <para>Remove the lubricant which is more than the necessary.</para>
               </proceduralStep>
            </proceduralStep>
         </mainProcedure>
         <closeRqmts>
            <reqCondGroup>
               <noConds />
            </reqCondGroup>
         </closeRqmts>
      </procedure>

Remove the lighting system from the packaging. Make sure that the components in the package are the same as those on the Install the light bulb to the front and rear lights (refer to ). Attach the front light fitting on the top of the handlebar. Apply the protective strip around the handlebar. Pull the clamp open and put it around the protective strip with the light connector at the top. Install the washer on the screw. Use the correct screwdriver from the and tighten the screw into the hole at the bottom of the clamp. This safeties the clamp to the handlebar. Attach the rear light fitting to the rear triangle of the bike frame. Apply the protective strip around one of the two rear triangle up-tubes. Pull the clamp open and put it around the protective strip. Make sure the light connector points rearwards. Install the washer on the screw. Use the correct screwdriver from the and tighten the screw into the hole at the bottom of the clamp. This safeties the clamp to the tube. Attach the light with the white glass to the front connector. Attach the light with the red glass to the rear connector. Installation of the circuit breaker Refer to figure Circuit Breaker/> For Mountain bike Storm type: Install the on the right hand bike handlebar using the clamping ring. Connect the circuit breaker electrical wire to the rear connector of the front light. Attach the wire to the frame with protective strip. For Mountain bike Trekker type: Install the on the left hand bike handlebar using the clamping ring. Connect the circuit breaker electrical wire to the rear connector of the front light. Attach the wire to the frame with protective strip.

      </reasonForUpdate>
