  <content>
    <description>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>General</title>
        <para>The <emphasis>s1kd-aspp</emphasis> tool has two main functions:</para>
        <para>
          <randomList>
            <listItem>
              <para>Generates display text for applicability statements. The text is derived from the logic described by the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12">assert</verbatimText> and <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12">evaluate</verbatimText> elements.</para>
            </listItem>
            <listItem>
              <para>Preprocesses "semantic" applicability statements in a data module to produce "presentation" applicability statements which are simpler to parse in an XSLT stylesheet.</para>
            </listItem>
          </randomList>
        </para>
        <para>"Semantic" applicability statements are those entered by the author to encode the applicability of elements within a data module. "Presentation" applicability statements are those that are actually displayed in page-oriented output, also referred to as the "human-readable" statements.</para>
        <para>The applicability in the resulting XML is longer semantically correct, but an XSLT stylesheet can simply place a statement on any element with attribute <extra_id_4 verbatimStyle="vs13">applicRefId</extra_id_4> without needing to consider inherited applicability statements on elements without the attribute.</para>
      </levelledPara>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>Usage</title>
        <extra_id_5>
          <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs24">s1kd-aspp [options] [<object> ...]</verbatimText>
        </extra_id_5>
      </levelledPara>
      <extra_id_6>
        <extra_id_7>Options</extra_id_7>
        <para>
          <definitionList>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-., --dump-disptext</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Dump the built-in .disptext file.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-,, --dump-xsl</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Dump the built-in XSLT used to generate display text for applicability statements.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-A, --act <ACT></listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_8>
                <para>Add an ACT to use when generating display text for product attributes. Multiple ACT data modules can be used by specifying this option multiple times.</para>
              </extra_id_8>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-a, --id <ID></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <extra_id_9>The ID to use for the inline applicability annotation representing the whole data module's applicability. Default is "app-0000".</extra_id_9>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-C, --cct <CCT></listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_10>
                <para>Add a CCT to use when generating display text for conditions. Multiple CCT data modules can be used by specifying this option multiple times.</para>
              </extra_id_10>
            </definitionListItem>
            <extra_id_11>
              <listItemTerm>-c, --search</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Search for the ACT and CCT referenced by each data module, and add them to the list of ACTs/CCTs to use when generating display text for that data module.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </extra_id_11>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-D, --delete</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Remove the display text from all applicability annotations, except those that consist of only display text (and no computer processing part).</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-d, --dir <dir></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Directory to start searching for ACT/CCT data modules in. By default, the current directory is used.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-F, --format <fmt></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Use a custom format string to generate display text.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <extra_id_12>-f, --overwrite</extra_id_12>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Overwrite input data module(s) rather than outputting to stdout.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-G, --disptext <disptext></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Specify a custom .disptext file.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <extra_id_13>
              <listItemTerm>-g, --generate</listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_14>
                <para>Generate display text for applicability statements.</para>
              </extra_id_14>
            </extra_id_13>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-h, -?, --help</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Show help/usage message.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <extra_id_15>-k, --keep</extra_id_15>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <extra_id_16>When generating display text, do not overwrite existing display text on statements, only generate display text for statements which have none.</extra_id_16>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-l, --list</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Treat input (stdin or arguments) as lists of filenames of objects, rather than objects themselves.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-N, --omit-issue</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Assume that the filenames for the ACT and CCT do not include issue info, i.e. they were created using the -N option of the s1kd-newdm tool.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-p, --presentation</listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_17>
                <para>Preprocess applicability statements to produce "presentation" applicability statements which are simpler to parse in an XSLT stylesheet. The applicability in the resulting XML is no longer semantically correct.</para>
              </extra_id_17>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-r, --recursive</listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_18>
                <para>Search for ACT/CCT data modules recursively.</para>
              </extra_id_18>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-t, --tags <mode></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Add tags before elements containing the display text of the applicability annotation they reference, simulating the typical presentation of applicability annotations within the XML.</para>
                <para>If <mode> is "pi", the tags are inserted as processing instructions, named "s1kd-aspp". This allows existing tags to be removed automatically before adding new ones.</para>
                <para>If <mode> is "comment", the tags are inserted as XML comments. Existing comments will not be removed automatically.</para>
                <extra_id_19>If <mode> is "remove", tags will be removed without adding new ones. This only applies to the processing instruction tags.</extra_id_19>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-v, --verbose</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <extra_id_20>Verbose output.</extra_id_20>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-x, --xsl <XSLT></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Use custom XSLT to generate display text for applicability statements.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>--version</listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_21>
                <para>Show version information.</para>
              </extra_id_21>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <extra_id_22><object> ...</extra_id_22>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>The object(s) to preprocess. This can include both individual objects and combined files such as those produced by s1kd-flatten(1).</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
          </definitionList>
        </para>
        <para>
          In addition, the following options allow configuration of the XML parser:
          <definitionList><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--dtdload</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Load the external DTD.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--huge</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Remove any internal arbitrary parser limits.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--net</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><extra_id_23>Allow network access to load external DTD and entities.</extra_id_23></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--noent</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Resolve entities.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--parser-errors</listItemTerm><extra_id_24><para>Emit errors from parser.</para></extra_id_24></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><extra_id_25>--parser-warnings</extra_id_25><listItemDefinition><para>Emit warnings from parser.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--xinclude</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Do XInclude processing.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem changeMark="1" changeType="add" reasonForUpdateRefIds="rfu-xml-catalog"><listItemTerm>--xml-catalog <file></listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Use an XML catalog when resolving entities. Multiple catalogs may be loaded by specifying this option multiple times.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem></definitionList>
        </para>
        <levelledPara>
          <title><verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.disptext</verbatimText> file</title>
          <extra_id_26>
            This file specifies rules for generating display text. It consists of:
            <randomList><listItem><para>operator rules</para></listItem><extra_id_27><para>property rules</para></extra_id_27></randomList>
          </extra_id_26>
          <para>The <extra_id_28 verbatimStyle="vs12"><operators></extra_id_28> element specifies the format of operators used in display text:
            <definitionList><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>and</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><extra_id_29>Text to use for the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs14">and</verbatimText> operator between assertions. Default is " and ".</extra_id_29></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><extra_id_30><listItemTerm>or</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Text to use for the <extra_id_31 verbatimStyle="vs14">or</extra_id_31> operator between assertions. Default is " or ".</para></listItemDefinition></extra_id_30><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>openGroup</listItemTerm><extra_id_32><para>Text to use to open a group of assertions. Default is "(".</para></extra_id_32></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>closeGroup</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Text to use to close a group of assertions. Default is ")".</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>set</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Text to use between items in a set (a|b|c).</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>range</listItemTerm><extra_id_33><para>Text to use between the start and end of a range (a~c).</para></extra_id_33></definitionListItem></definitionList>
          </para>
          <para>Each <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><property></verbatimText> element specifies the format used for an individual property. The <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><productAttributes></verbatimText> and <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><conditions></verbatimText> elements specify the default format for product attributes and conditions that are not listed. Alternatively, the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><default></verbatimText> element specifies the default format for both product attributes and conditions together.</para>
          <para>The format is specified using a combination of the following elements:
            <definitionList><definitionListItem><listItemTerm><name></listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Replaced by the name of the property.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><extra_id_34><listItemTerm><text></listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Text that is included as-is.</para></listItemDefinition></extra_id_34><definitionListItem><listItemTerm><values></listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Replaced by the values specified for the property in the applicability assertion.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem></definitionList>
          </para>
          <para>Optionally, <extra_id_35 verbatimStyle="vs12"><values></extra_id_35> may contain a list of custom labels for individual values. Any values not included in this list will use their normal label.</para>
          <para>By default, the program will search for a file named <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.disptext</verbatimText> in the current directory and parent directories, but any file can be specified using the -G (--disptext) option.</para>
          <para>Example of a <extra_id_36 verbatimStyle="vs02">.disptext</extra_id_36> file:</para>
          <extra_id_37>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><disptext>
<operators>
<and> + </and>
<or>, </or>
<openGroup>[</openGroup>
<closeGroup>]</closeGroup>
<set> or </set>
<range> thru </range>
</operators>
<default>
<name/>
<text>: </text>
<values/>
</default>
<property ident="model" type="prodattr">
<values>
<value match="BRKTRKR">Brook trekker</value>
<value match="MNTSTRM">Mountain storm</value>
</values>
<text> </text>
<name/>
</property>
</disptext></verbatimText>
          </extra_id_37>
          <para>Given the above example, the following display would be generated for each annotation:</para>
          <para>
            Assert annotation:
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><assert
applicPropertyIdent="model"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="BRKTRKR"/></verbatimText>
            Human-readable format:
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs23">"Brook trekker Model"</verbatimText>
          </para>
          <extra_id_38>
            Evaluate annotation:
            <extra_id_39 verbatimStyle="vs11"><evaluate andOr="or">
<evaluate andOr="and">
<assert
applicPropertyIdent="model"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="BRKTRKR"/>
<assert
applicPropertyIdent="version"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="Mk1"/>
</evaluate>
<evaluate andOr="and">
<assert
applicPropertyIdent="model"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="MNTSTRM"/>
<assert
applicPropertyIdent="version"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="Mk9"/>
</evaluate>
</evaluate></extra_id_39>
            Human-readable format:
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs23">"[Brook trekker Model + Version: Mk9],
[Mountain storm Model + Version: Mk1]"</verbatimText>
          </extra_id_38>
          <extra_id_40>
            Evaluate annotation:
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><evaluate andOr="and">
<assert
applicPropertyIdent="model"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="BRKTRKR|MNTSTRM"/>
<assert
applicPropertyIdent="version"
applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="Mk1~Mk9"/>
</evaluate></verbatimText>
            Human-readable format:
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs23">"Brook trekker or Mountain storm Model + Version: Mk1 thru Mk9"</verbatimText>
          </extra_id_40>
        </levelledPara>
      </extra_id_6>
      <levelledPara>
        <extra_id_41>Examples</extra_id_41>
        <levelledPara>
          <title>Generating display text</title>
          <para>The built-in XSLT for generating display text follows the guidance in Chap 7.8 of the S1000D 5.0 specification. For example, given the following:</para>
          <para>
            <extra_id_42 verbatimStyle="vs11"><applic>
<assert applicPropertyIdent="prodversion"
applicPropertyType="prodattr" applicPropertyValues="A"/>
</applic></extra_id_42>
          </para>
          <para>The resulting XML would contain:</para>
          <para>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><applic>
<displayText>
<simplePara>prodversion: A</simplePara>
</displayText>
<assert applicPropertyIdent="prodversion"
applicPropertyType="prodattr" applicPropertyValues="A"/>
</applic></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <para>If ACTs or CCTs are supplied which define display names for a property, this will be used instead of the ident. For example, the ACT defines the display name for the "<extra_id_43 verbatimStyle="vs14">prodversion</extra_id_43>" product attribute:</para>
          <para>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><productAttribute id="prodversion">
<name>Product version</name>
<displayName>Version</displayName>
<descr>The version of the product.</descr>
<enumeration applicPropertyValues="A|B|C"/>
</productAttribute></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <extra_id_44>When supplied with the -A option:</extra_id_44>
          <para>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs24">$ s1kd-aspp -g -A <ACT> <DM></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <para>The resulting XML would instead contain:</para>
          <para>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><applic>
<displayText>
<simplePara>Version: A</simplePara>
<assert applicPropertyIdent="prodversion"
applicPropertyType="prodattr" applicPropertyValues="A"/>
</displayText>
</applic></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <para changeMark="1" changeType="modify" reasonForUpdateRefIds="rfu-0001">The methods for generating display text can be changed either via the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.disptext</verbatimText> file, or by supplying a custom XSLT script with the -x option. The -, option can be used to dump the built-in XSLT as a starting point for a custom script.</para>
        </levelledPara>
        <levelledPara>
          <title>Display text format string (-F)</title>
          <para>The -F option allows for very simple customizations to generated display text without needing to create a custom <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.disptext</verbatimText> file or XSLT script (-x). The string determines the format of the display text of each <extra_id_45 verbatimStyle="vs12"><assert></extra_id_45> element in the annotation.</para>
          <extra_id_46>The following variables can be used within the format string:
            <definitionList><extra_id_47><listItemTerm>%name%</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>The name of the property.</para></listItemDefinition></extra_id_47><extra_id_48><listItemTerm>%values%</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><extra_id_49>The applicable value(s) of the property.</extra_id_49></listItemDefinition></extra_id_48></definitionList>
          </extra_id_46>
          <para>For example:
            <extra_id_50 verbatimStyle="vs24">$ s1kd-aspp -g <DM>
...
<applic>
<displayText>
<simplePara>Version: A</simplePara>
</displayText>
<assert applicPropertyIdent="version" applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="A"/>
</applic>
...

$ s1kd-aspp -F '%name% = %values%' -g <DM>
...
<applic>
<displayText>
<simplePara>Version = A</simplePara>
</displayText>
<assert applicPropertyIdent="version" applicPropertyType="prodattr"
applicPropertyValues="A"/>
</applic>
...</extra_id_50>
          </para>
        </levelledPara>
        <levelledPara>
          <title>Creating presentation applicability statements</title>
          <para>Given the following:</para>
          <para>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><dmodule>
<identAndStatusSection>
<dmAddress>...</dmAddress>
<dmStatus>
...
<applic>
<displayText>
<simplePara>A or B</simplePara>
</displayText>
</applic>
...
</dmStatus>
</identAndStatusSection>
<content>
<referencedApplicGroup>
<applic id="app-B">
<displayText>
<simplePara>B</simplePara>
</displayText>
</applic>
</referencedApplicGroup>
<procedure>
<preliminaryRqmts>...</preliminaryRqmts>
<mainProcedure>
<proceduralStep>
<para>This step is applicable to A or B.</para>
</proceduralStep>
<proceduralStep applicRefId="app-B">
<para>This step is applicable to B only.</para>
</proceduralStep>
<proceduralStep applicRefId="app-B">
<para>This step is also applicable to B only.</para>
</proceduralStep>
<proceduralStep>
<para>This step is also applicable to A or B.</para>
</proceduralStep>
</mainProcedure>
<closeRqmts>...</closeRqmts>
</procedure>
</content>
</dmodule></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <para>Applicability statements should be displayed whenever applicability changes:</para>
          <para>
            <sequentialList>
              <listItem>
                <para>This step is applicable to A or B.</para>
              </listItem>
              <extra_id_51>
                <para>
                  <emphasis>Applicable to: B</emphasis>
                </para>
                <para>This step is applicable to B only.</para>
              </extra_id_51>
              <listItem>
                <para>This step is also applicable to B only.</para>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <extra_id_52>
                  <emphasis>Applicable to: A or B</emphasis>
                </extra_id_52>
                <para>This step is also applicable to A or B.</para>
              </listItem>
            </sequentialList>
          </para>
          <para>There are two parts which are difficult to do in an XSLT stylesheet:</para>
          <para>
            <extra_id_53>
              <listItem>
                <para>No statement is shown on Step 3 despite having attribute <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs13">applicRefId</verbatimText> because the applicability has not changed since the last statement on Step 2.</para>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <para>A statement is shown on Step 4 despite not having attribute <extra_id_54 verbatimStyle="vs13">applicRefId</extra_id_54> because the applicability has changed back to that of the whole data module.</para>
              </listItem>
            </extra_id_53>
          </para>
          <para>Using the s1kd-aspp tool, the above XML would produce the following output:</para>
          <para>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs11"><dmodule>
<identAndStatusSection>
<dmAddress>...</dmAddress>
<dmStatus>
...
<applic>
<displayText>
<simplePara>A or B</simplePara>
</displayText>
</applic>
...
</dmStatus>
</identAndStatusSection>
<content>
<referencedApplicGroup>
<applic id="app-B">
<displayText>
<simplePara>B</simplePara>
</displayText>
</applic>
<applic id="app-0000">
<displayText>
<simplePara>A or B</simplePara>
</displayText>
</applic>
</referencedApplicGroup>
<procedure>
<preliminaryRqmts>...</preliminaryRqmts>
<mainProcedure>
<proceduralStep>
<para>This step is applicable to A or B.</para>
</proceduralStep>
<proceduralStep applicRefId="app-B">
<para>This step is applicable to B only.</para>
</proceduralStep>
<proceduralStep>
<para>This step is also applicable to B only.</para>
</proceduralStep>
<proceduralStep applicRefId="app-0000">
<para>This step is also applicable to A or B.</para>
</proceduralStep>
</mainProcedure>
</procedure>
</content>
</dmodule></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <para>With attribute <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs13">applicRefId</verbatimText> only on those elements where a statement should be shown, and an additional inline applicability to represent the whole data module's applicability. This XML is semantically incorrect but easier for a stylesheet to transform for page-oriented output.</para>
        </levelledPara>
      </levelledPara>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>Display text rules schema</title>
        <levelledPara>
          <extra_id_55>Display text rules</extra_id_55>
          <para>The element <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><disptext></verbatimText> contains all the rules for the formatting of generated display text in applicability annotations.</para>
          <para>
            <emphasis>Markup element:</emphasis>
            <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><disptext></verbatimText>
          </para>
          <para>
            <emphasis>Attributes:</emphasis>
          </para>
          <para>
            <randomList>
              <listItem>
                <para>None</para>
              </listItem>
            </randomList>
          </para>
          <para>
            <extra_id_56>Child elements:</extra_id_56>
          </para>
          <para>
            <randomList>
              <listItem>
                <para>
                  <extra_id_57 verbatimStyle="vs12"><operators></extra_id_57>
                </para>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <para>
                  <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><default></verbatimText>
                </para>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <para>
                  <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><productAttributes></verbatimText>
                </para>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <extra_id_58>
                  <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><conditions></verbatimText>
                </extra_id_58>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <para>
                  <extra_id_59 verbatimStyle="vs12"><conditionType></extra_id_59>
                </para>
              </listItem>
              <listItem>
                <para>
                  <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs12"><property></verbatimText>

    <refs>
      <dmRef>
        <dmRefIdent>
          <dmCode modelIdentCode="S1KDTOOLS" systemDiffCode="A" systemCode="07" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="A" infoCode="040" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="D" />
        </dmRefIdent>

            <infoName>Description</infoName>
          </dmTitle>
        </dmRefAddressItems>
      </dmRef>
    </refs>
    <description>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>General</title>
        <para>The <emphasis>s1kd-newupf</emphasis> tool creates a new S1000D data update file for two specified issues of a CIR data module. Changes to items between the source and target issues of the CIR are recorded in the resulting UPF, along with update instructions.</para>
      </levelledPara>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>Usage</title>
        <para>
          <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs24">s1kd-newupf [options] <SOURCE> <TARGET></verbatimText>
        </para>
      </levelledPara>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>Options</title>
        <para>
          <definitionList>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-$, --issue <issue></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Specify which issue of S1000D to use. Currently supported issues are:</para>
                <para>
                  <randomList>
                    <listItem>
                      <para>5.0 (default)</para>
                    </listItem>
                    <listItem>
                      <para>4.2</para>
                    </listItem>
                    <listItem>
                      <para>4.1</para>
                    </listItem>
                  </randomList>
                </para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-@, --out <path></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Save the new update file to <path>. If <path> is an existing directory, the update file will be created in it instead of the current directory. Otherwise, the update file will be saved as the filename <path> instead of being automatically named.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-%, --templates <dir></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Use XML template in the specified directory instead of the built-in template. The template must be named <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">update.xml</verbatimText> in the directory <dir>, and must conform to the default S1000D issue of this tool (5.0).</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-~, --dump-templates <dir></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Dump the built-in XML template to the specified directory.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-d, --defaults <file></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Specify the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.defaults</verbatimText> file name.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-f, --overwrite</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Overwrite existing file.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-h, -?, --help</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Show help/usage message.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-q, --quiet</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Do not report an error when the file already exists.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-v, --verbose</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Print the file name of the newly created data update file.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>--version</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Show version information.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm><SOURCE></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>The source (original) issue of the CIR data module.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm><TARGET></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>The target (updated) issue of the CIR data module.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
          </definitionList>
        </para>
        <para>
          In addition, the following options allow configuration of the XML parser:
          <definitionList><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--dtdload</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Load the external DTD.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--huge</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Remove any internal arbitrary parser limits.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--net</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Allow network access to load external DTD and entities.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--noent</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Resolve entities.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--parser-errors</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Emit errors from parser.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--parser-warnings</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Emit warnings from parser.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--xinclude</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Do XInclude processing.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><definitionListItem changeMark="1" changeType="add" reasonForUpdateRefIds="rfu-xml-catalog"><listItemTerm>--xml-catalog <file></listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Use an XML catalog when resolving entities. Multiple catalogs may be loaded by specifying this option multiple times.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem></definitionList>
        </para>
        <levelledPara>
          <title><verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.defaults</verbatimText> file</title>
          <para>Refer to <dmRef><dmRefIdent><dmCode modelIdentCode="S1KDTOOLS" systemDiffCode="A" systemCode="07" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="A" infoCode="040" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="D" /></dmRefIdent><dmRefAddressItems><dmTitle><techName>s1kd-newdm</techName><infoName>Description</infoName></dmTitle></dmRefAddressItems></dmRef> for information on the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.defaults</verbatimText> file which is used by all the s1kd-new* commands.</para>
        </levelledPara>
      </levelledPara>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>Example</title>
        <para>
          <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs24">$ s1kd-newupf \
    DMC-EX-A-00-00-00-00A-00GA-D_001-00_EN-CA.XML \
    DMC-EX-A-00-00-00-00A-00GA-D_002-00_EN-CA.XML</verbatimText>
        </para>
      </levelledPara>
    </description>
  </content>
</dmodule>

      <levelledPara>
        <extra_id_16>General</extra_id_16>
        <extra_id_17>The <extra_id_18>s1kd-newupf</extra_id_18> tool creates a new S1000D data update file for two specified issues of a CIR data module. Changes to items between the source and target issues of the CIR are recorded in the resulting UPF, along with update instructions.</extra_id_17>
      </levelledPara>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>Usage</title>
        <para>
          <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs24">s1kd-newupf [options] <SOURCE> <TARGET></verbatimText>
        </para>
      </levelledPara>
      <extra_id_19>
        <title>Options</title>
        <para>
          <definitionList>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-$, --issue <issue></listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Specify which issue of S1000D to use. Currently supported issues are:</para>
                <para>
                  <randomList>
                    <extra_id_20>
                      <extra_id_21>5.0 (default)</extra_id_21>
                    </extra_id_20>
                    <extra_id_22>
                      <para>4.2</para>
                    </extra_id_22>
                    <extra_id_23>
                      <para>4.1</para>
                    </extra_id_23>
                  </randomList>
                </para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <extra_id_24>
              <listItemTerm>-@, --out <path></listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_25>
                <extra_id_26>Save the new update file to <path>. If <path> is an existing directory, the update file will be created in it instead of the current directory. Otherwise, the update file will be saved as the filename <path> instead of being automatically named.</extra_id_26>
              </extra_id_25>
            </extra_id_24>
            <extra_id_27>
              <extra_id_28>-%, --templates <dir></extra_id_28>
              <extra_id_29>
                <para>Use XML template in the specified directory instead of the built-in template. The template must be named <extra_id_30 verbatimStyle="vs02">update.xml</extra_id_30> in the directory <dir>, and must conform to the default S1000D issue of this tool (5.0).</para>
              </extra_id_29>
            </extra_id_27>
            <definitionListItem>
              <extra_id_31>-~, --dump-templates <dir></extra_id_31>
              <extra_id_32>
                <extra_id_33>Dump the built-in XML template to the specified directory.</extra_id_33>
              </extra_id_32>
            </definitionListItem>
            <extra_id_34>
              <extra_id_35>-d, --defaults <file></extra_id_35>
              <extra_id_36>
                <extra_id_37>Specify the <extra_id_38 verbatimStyle="vs02">.defaults</extra_id_38> file name.</extra_id_37>
              </extra_id_36>
            </extra_id_34>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>-f, --overwrite</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Overwrite existing file.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <extra_id_39>
              <extra_id_40>-h, -?, --help</extra_id_40>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <extra_id_41>Show help/usage message.</extra_id_41>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </extra_id_39>
            <definitionListItem>
              <extra_id_42>-q, --quiet</extra_id_42>
              <extra_id_43>
                <para>Do not report an error when the file already exists.</para>
              </extra_id_43>
            </definitionListItem>
            <extra_id_44>
              <listItemTerm>-v, --verbose</listItemTerm>
              <extra_id_45>
                <extra_id_46>Print the file name of the newly created data update file.</extra_id_46>
              </extra_id_45>
            </extra_id_44>
            <extra_id_47>
              <extra_id_48>--version</extra_id_48>
              <extra_id_49>
                <para>Show version information.</para>
              </extra_id_49>
            </extra_id_47>
            <extra_id_50>
              <extra_id_51><SOURCE></extra_id_51>
              <extra_id_52>
                <extra_id_53>The source (original) issue of the CIR data module.</extra_id_53>
              </extra_id_52>
            </extra_id_50>
            <definitionListItem>
              <extra_id_54><TARGET></extra_id_54>
              <extra_id_55>
                <extra_id_56>The target (updated) issue of the CIR data module.</extra_id_56>
              </extra_id_55>
            </definitionListItem>
          </definitionList>
        </para>
        <extra_id_57>
          In addition, the following options allow configuration of the XML parser:
          <definitionList><extra_id_58><extra_id_59>--dtdload</extra_id_59><listItemDefinition><para>Load the external DTD.</para></listItemDefinition></extra_id_58><extra_id_60><listItemTerm>--huge</listItemTerm><extra_id_61><para>Remove any internal arbitrary parser limits.</para></extra_id_61></extra_id_60><definitionListItem><extra_id_62>--net</extra_id_62><listItemDefinition><extra_id_63>Allow network access to load external DTD and entities.</extra_id_63></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><extra_id_64><listItemTerm>--noent</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><extra_id_65>Resolve entities.</extra_id_65></listItemDefinition></extra_id_64><definitionListItem><listItemTerm>--parser-errors</listItemTerm><extra_id_66><extra_id_67>Emit errors from parser.</extra_id_67></extra_id_66></definitionListItem><definitionListItem><extra_id_68>--parser-warnings</extra_id_68><listItemDefinition><extra_id_69>Emit warnings from parser.</extra_id_69></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem><extra_id_70><listItemTerm>--xinclude</listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Do XInclude processing.</para></listItemDefinition></extra_id_70><definitionListItem changeMark="1" changeType="add" reasonForUpdateRefIds="rfu-xml-catalog"><listItemTerm>--xml-catalog <file></listItemTerm><listItemDefinition><para>Use an XML catalog when resolving entities. Multiple catalogs may be loaded by specifying this option multiple times.</para></listItemDefinition></definitionListItem></definitionList>
        </extra_id_57>
        <levelledPara>
          <title><extra_id_71 verbatimStyle="vs02">.defaults</extra_id_71> file</title>
          <para>Refer to <extra_id_72><dmRefIdent><extra_id_73 modelIdentCode="S1KDTOOLS" systemDiffCode="A" systemCode="07" subSystemCode="0" subSubSystemCode="0" assyCode="00" disassyCode="00" disassyCodeVariant="A" infoCode="040" infoCodeVariant="A" itemLocationCode="D" /></dmRefIdent><extra_id_74><extra_id_75><techName>s1kd-newdm</techName><infoName>Description</infoName></extra_id_75></extra_id_74></extra_id_72> for information on the <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs02">.defaults</verbatimText> file which is used by all the s1kd-new* commands.</para>
        </levelledPara>
      </extra_id_19>
      <extra_id_76>
        <extra_id_77>Example</extra_id_77>
        <extra_id_78>
          <verbatimText verbatimStyle="vs24">$ s1kd-newupf \
    DMC-EX-A-00-00-00-00A-00GA-D_001-00_EN-CA.XML \
    DMC-EX-A-00-00-00-00A-00GA-D_002-00_EN-CA.XML</verbatimText>
        </extra_id_78>
      </extra_id_76>
    </description>

    <description>
      <levelledPara>
        <title>General</title>
        <para>This document summarizes the compatibility between the s1kd-tools and each issue of the S1000D specification for which support is planned.</para>
        <para>
          <definitionList>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>[empty]</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Support is planned but not yet implemented.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>X</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Support is implemented.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>/</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Support is partially implemented.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>~</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Support is not planned. Usually this is because older issues of the specification did not cover the function of the tool.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
          </definitionList>
        </para>
        <note>
          <notePara>Although a tool may not directly support an issue of S1000D, it may still be possible to use with that issue.</notePara>
          <notePara>For example, the s1kd-brexcheck tool is said not to support Issue 2.0 or Issue 2.1, because the BREX data module schema was not introduced until Issue 2.2. However, an Issue 2.2 or greater BREX data module can still be used to check Issue 2.0 or Issue 2.1 CSDB objects.</notePara>
        </note>
      </levelledPara>

        <title>General</title>
        <extra_id_1>This document summarizes the compatibility between the s1kd-tools and each issue of the S1000D specification for which support is planned.</extra_id_1>
        <para>

                <extra_id_3>Support is partially implemented.</extra_id_3>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>
            <definitionListItem>
              <listItemTerm>~</listItemTerm>
              <listItemDefinition>
                <para>Support is not planned. Usually this is because older issues of the specification did not cover the function of the tool.</para>
              </listItemDefinition>
            </definitionListItem>

        </para>
        <note>
          <notePara>Although a tool may not directly support an issue of S1000D, it may still be possible to use with that issue.</notePara>
